ip_top_stories.title: Publishers Back Concord Music Group's AI Suit
ip_top_stories.summary: Publishers and media groups have filed in support of Concord Music Group's lawsuit against Anthropic, according to Publishers Weekly. The case centres on AI training data and copyright infringement claims against the AI company.

ip_top_stories.title: German Children's Book Publisher Sues OpenAI Over Copyright
ip_top_stories.summary: A German children's book publisher has filed a copyright lawsuit against OpenAI, adding to the growing number of publishing industry legal actions against AI companies over training data use.

ip_top_stories.title: UK Government Maintains Status Quo on AI and Copyright, Playing the Long Game on Potential Reform
ip_top_stories.summary: The UK government has opted against its previously preferred proposal on AI and copyright, maintaining the current legal framework while signalling potential future reform. The decision has been characterised by legal commentators as a deferral rather than a resolution of the underlying policy tensions.

ip_top_stories.title: Researchers Challenge OpenAI Defence After Claiming ChatGPT Can Output Near-Verbatim Copies of Published Books
ip_top_stories.summary: Researchers have published findings claiming ChatGPT is capable of reproducing near-verbatim passages from published books, directly challenging OpenAI's legal defence in copyright infringement cases. The findings could have significant implications for ongoing litigation involving book publishers.

ip_top_stories.title: What AI Asks of Open Access
ip_top_stories.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen examines how AI systems' reliance on openly accessible content is reshaping questions around open access publishing, raising new tensions between the goals of open knowledge dissemination and the commercial use of that content by AI developers.

ip_further_links.title: SCOTUS's Cox Ruling Could Impact Publishers' Fight Against AI
ip_further_links.summary: Publishers Weekly reports that the Supreme Court's Cox ruling on secondary liability may open new legal avenues for publishers pursuing copyright claims against AI companies and their LLMs.

ip_further_links.title: No Human, No Copyright: AI-Generated Works Remain Legally Unprotected as U.S. Law Stalls
ip_further_links.summary: A review of the current US legal position confirms that AI-generated works remain ineligible for copyright protection due to the human authorship requirement, with legislative reform showing no signs of progress.

ip_further_links.title: Axios AI+DC Summit: Copyright Protection in the AI Era Will Be Up to the Courts, Industry Leaders Say
ip_further_links.summary: Industry leaders speaking at the Axios AI+DC Summit said they expect courts rather than legislators to resolve the key copyright questions raised by AI, given the current pace of US legislative inaction.

ip_further_links.title: The House of Lords Has Spoken on AI and Copyright – Here Is What It Means for You
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of the UK House of Lords' position on AI and copyright and its practical implications for rightsholders and AI developers.

ip_further_links.title: Harlequin to Co-Produce AI-Generated 'Microdramas'
ip_further_links.summary: Harlequin has announced plans to co-produce a slate of AI-generated short-form video content, marking a notable move by a major publisher into generative AI content production.

ip_further_links.title: Copyright in AI Prompts: Chinese Court Ruling on Generative AI and Originality
ip_further_links.summary: A Chinese court has issued a ruling examining whether AI-generated outputs created via user prompts can attract copyright protection, with the decision hinging on questions of originality.

ip_further_links.title: Cloudflare Legal Chief on AI Bots and Publisher Revenue Loss
ip_further_links.summary: Cloudflare's general counsel discusses the impact of AI web crawlers on publisher revenue and the emerging technical and legal tools being considered to address the problem.

ip_further_links.title: How India Is Trying to Navigate AI Copyright's Three-Body Problem
ip_further_links.summary: An analysis of India's policy challenge in balancing the competing interests of AI developers, creators, and the public in its approach to AI copyright reform.

ip_further_links.title: AI and Publishing: FAQ for Writers
ip_further_links.summary: A practical FAQ addressing writers' key questions about AI's impact on publishing, covering copyright, contracts, and the use of AI tools in the creative process.

ip_further_links.title: Beyond Copyright: Why Asia Pacific Governments Must Govern AI Training Data as Public Infrastructure
ip_further_links.summary: A policy commentary arguing that Asia Pacific governments should treat AI training data governance as a matter of public infrastructure rather than leaving it solely to copyright law.
